newsitem.title: USA: Firm formed by Quayle group to be sold for $50 mln.
newsitem.headline: Firm formed by Quayle group to be sold for $50 mln.

text.p: IFS Financial Corp, a Woodlands, Texas, holding company, said Thursday it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Circle Investors Inc, an Indianapolis investment firm formed by a group led by former Vice President Dan Quayle.
The cash and stock deal is valued at $50.2 million and is subject to approval by state insurance regulators, IFS said.
The deal includes Circle Investors' four subvsidiaries led by American Founders Life Insurance Co, IFS said.
Hugo Pimienta, IFS chairman and chief executive officer, said IFS "remains committed to growth and expects the Circle acquisition to lead to others."
Plans call for American Founders and IFS' subsidiary Bradford National Life Insurance Co, an annuity specialist, to operate as units of IFS Circle Insurance Holdings Corp, which IFS owns, IFS said.

Circle's president and chief executive, Matthew Neff, will become president and CEO of IFS Circle while Douglas Pierce, chairman and CEO of Bradford National, will be chairman of IFS Circle and American Founders, it said.

American Founders, based in Phoenix, has $255 million in assets and $1.2 billion in life insurance in force. Other Circle companies in the deal are Liberty Bankers Life Insurance Co, of Ohio; Laurel Life Insurance Co, of Texas; and Aztec Life Insurance Co, of California, IFS said.

In addition to to Bradford National, which is based in New Orleans, IFS' major subsidiaries are AccuBanc Mortgage Corp, of Dallas; GAMMA Capital Corp and International Mortgage Resources Corp, both of Woodlands, Texas; and Structured Servicing Transactions Group, of New York.
